title: Some stories in the Bible feel small at first glance.
paragraphs: Some stories in the Bible feel small at first glance.

A few verses.
One man.
One moment.
But hidden inside them are truths that can reshape how you see yourself… and how you see God.
Ehud is one of those stories.
Israel had drifted again.
They did what was evil in the sight of the Lord, and as a result, they fell under the oppression of Moab (Judges 3:12). This wasn’t a quick setback. It lasted eighteen years.

Eighteen years of pressure.
Eighteen years of limitation.
Eighteen years of wondering if things would ever change.
And then something shifted.
“They cried unto the Lord…”
That’s where deliverance always begins.

Not with strength.
Not with strategy.
But with surrender.
And the Bible says, “The Lord raised them up a deliverer, Ehud…” (Judges 3:15).
Pause there.

God didn’t just send help.
He raised a person.
And that person didn’t look like the obvious choice.
Ehud was left-handed.

In that time, that wasn’t just a random detail. It made him different in a world built around right-handed strength. Most warriors trained, fought, and carried weapons in a way that assumed right-hand dominance.
Ehud didn’t fit that mold.
But what made him different… made him effective.
Let that settle.
Because some of you have spent years trying to fix what God may have designed.

You’ve tried to blend in.
Tried to adjust.
Tried to become more “normal.”

But God is not looking for copies.
He works through design.
Ehud’s left hand wasn’t a weakness in God’s eyes.
It was part of the plan.
The Bible says Ehud made a double-edged dagger and strapped it to his right thigh (Judges 3:16). That detail matters.
Why?
Because guards expected weapons on the left side, drawn by the right hand.
Ehud didn’t fit the expectation.
And because of that, he passed through unnoticed.
What people didn’t expect… God had already prepared.
This is where the lesson gets deeper.

Your difference is not just identity.
It may be strategy.

The way you think.
The way you process.
The way you’ve lived.
Even the things that made you feel out of place…
God can position all of it for purpose.

Ehud gained access to King Eglon.
He stood in a private moment that no one else had.
And in that moment, he acted.

Now, let’s be clear—this is a historical account of deliverance during a specific time in Israel’s history. It is not a command for us to imitate his actions. But it does reveal how God can use a person, in their context, to bring about freedom.
Ehud moved with courage.

He didn’t freeze in fear.
He didn’t shrink in doubt.
He stepped into the assignment placed in front of him.
And everything changed.
After that moment, Ehud escaped, rallied Israel, and led them into victory over Moab (Judges 3:27–29).
And then comes a line that should stop you:
“So Moab was subdued that day… And the land had rest for eighty years.” (Judges 3:30)
Eighty years of peace.
Let that sink in.

One life.
Raised by God.
Willing to act.
Changed the trajectory of a nation for generations.
That is the weight of obedience.

We often think our lives are small.
Our actions are insignificant.
Our obedience doesn’t matter that much.
But Scripture shows us something different.

God can take one surrendered person…
and use them to bring freedom far beyond what they can see.
So the question is not:
“Am I the most qualified?”
Ehud wasn’t.
The question is:
“Am I willing to be used?”
Because God is not limited by what people expect.

He is not restricted by your background.
He is not intimidated by your differences.
He is not searching for perfection.
He is looking for availability.
And sometimes…

The thing you thought disqualified you
is the very thing He designed to position you.

Ehud didn’t become someone else.
He didn’t try to match the system around him.
He allowed God to use who he was.
And through that, deliverance came.

So before you dismiss your story…
before you hide what makes you different…
before you assume God can’t use you…
Remember this:
God often hides His strategy inside what the world overlooks.

You are not disqualified because you are different.
You are not forgotten because you are unseen.
You are not useless because you don’t fit expectations.
You may be positioned.
And when your moment comes…
Will you step forward?
Because your obedience might not just change your life.
It might bring freedom to others too.
Memorable lines to carry with you:

What people overlook, God often prepares.
Your difference may be part of your assignment.
God doesn’t need the obvious—He uses the available.
Hidden does not mean useless.
One act of obedience can echo for generations.

Engagement Question:
What is something in your life you once saw as a weakness… that God might actually want to use?
